definitions.gloss: to complete; to finish; to be completed
definitions.explanation: To bring something to its finished state, or for something to reach completion. Can be used both transitively (to complete something) and intransitively (something is completed).

examples.japanese: {作品|さくひん}が{完成|かんせい}した。
{新|あたら}しいビルは{来年|らいねん}{完成|かんせい}する{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: The new building is scheduled to be completed next year.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}か{月|げつ}かけてようやくこの{絵|え}を{完成|かんせい}させた。
examples.english: I finally completed this painting after spending three months on it.

notes:
{完成|かんせい}する is used when something reaches its finished, polished state. It often implies a significant undertaking — a building, artwork, product, or project — rather than a simple everyday task. The intransitive pattern ～が{完成|かんせい}する is more common than the transitive ～を{完成|かんせい}する; the causative ～を{完成|かんせい}させる is preferred for transitive use.

USAGE:
- Intransitive: {作品|さくひん}が{完成|かんせい}する (the work is completed)
- Transitive (causative preferred): {作品|さくひん}を{完成|かんせい}させる (to complete the work)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビルが{完成|かんせい}する: a building is completed
- {作品|さくひん}を{完成|かんせい}させる: to complete a work
- {完成|かんせい}{予定|よてい}: scheduled completion
- {完成|かんせい}{間近|まぢか}: nearing completion
- {完成|かんせい}{品|ひん}: finished product

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仕上|しあ}げる: to finish up — focuses on the final touches or finishing process
- {終了|しゅうりょう}する: to end; to conclude — marks the end of a process or event, not necessarily the creation of something
- {達成|たっせい}する: to achieve; to accomplish — emphasizes reaching a goal rather than finishing a creation
